The Ecology of the Wealdwoods
Trespassing Among Ancients
Stepping into a clearing, a ray of sunlight pierces the leaf coverage above and alights on a bed of fern and flowers, the rich gold and greens beckon the 
Traveler into a sanctuary of safety. Motes of pollen dance in the faint breeze, with only the song of birds from above to break the otherwise gentle silence. 
Closing their eyes but for a brief moment, the Traveler lets out a long held breath, feeling a sort of peace and oneness with the land comes over them. 
Suddenly a twig breaks and the Traveler’s eyes open with a snap to find four sets of yellow eyes staring from the shadows at the clearing's edge.
With spear held tight, feet planted firmly and the Traveler readies themselves to be charged. A few rapid heartbeats pass, then more, and the tension in 
their shoulders lessen as the distant eyes blink but approach no further, a sense of curiosity is felt from the staring and slowly the Traveler turns their 
spear tip downward into the soft loamy earth and gently approaches with an open hand outstretched. 
Walking towards the wall of trees, shadowed bodies separate from the branches and beaks questioningly clatter. Four white feathered heads, tilt and 
turn to inspect the strange intruder in their wooded realm. Lithe forms drop from the branches and began prodding and pulling at the Traveler's cloak. 
Overcome with an unexpected joy, the Traveler quietly laughs at the reception, turning about to allow the avians to sate their innate curiosity. Finally 
breathing out a sigh of true relief, the Traveler pulls out their journal and begins to sketch the inquisitive calitross.
A primordial tension can be felt when stepping beneath the branches of the Wealdwoods, a rolling sea of trees that covers much of the 
eastern side of the island. Like the teeming reefs that crest the south, the woods are an ecosystem of vibrant flora and very territorial 
fauna. Through countless generations of fierce competition, from the fungus filled leaf litter, crawling with equal parts life and decay, 
to the nearly vertical living of vine choked towering tree trunks, to the sunlit canopy heights where the skies carry their own dangers. 
Life has ruthlessly fought for every inch of space, and the line that separates predator and prey blurs with the slightest misstep, a beast 
that prowls the branches above may fall to the ground and find themselves entering a wholly alien environment, mere dozens of feet 
from the niche they once dominated, at the mercy of ground dwelling scavengers that quickly approach.
Roots sink deep into the clear waters of this sunken Wealdwoods, the furthest eastern forest on Sol’Kesh. Tributaries run through these 
woods akin to veins and during spring there is hardly a patch of soil not under the flowing waters. Yet unlike the rotten bog woods 
found in the north, the running rivers present a clear, heady scent of fresh dew. Many fish and amphibians call the safety of these root-
twisted depths home, as the natural cover is an ideal nursery for young, keeping them safe from the larger predators such as murrow 
and the dreaded nuthorghull, and while safe from some, lithe and agile fish still haunt these waters. Vicious larkiera in particular, with 
their sinuous bodies and powerful fins can chase down most aquatic prey, weaving around the twisting confines with ease, and when 
the opportunity arises, breach the still surface to snatch unsuspecting frondilli.
Towering Life
To a Traveler, the Wealdwoods could be a near endless supply of 
resources in both plant and animal life to survive off of. Beyond 
the simple lumber of a felled tree, countless fungi invade the 
root, trunk and canopy above. Dozens of colorful specimens may 
supply a myriad of medicinal uses, or deadly poisons to those with 
the knowledge on how to make use of it, yet tread softly under 
these boughs. The raucous destruction of cutting down a tree or 
the heavy footfalls of a large party can attract undue attention. 
Scavengers roam along the ground as much as among the 
branches, and a fallen corpse rarely lasts a full night. Everything 
from scurrying scavick, cunning calitross, to winged basilospri 
will quickly strip the meat off the bones, leaving scraps that are 
readily consumed by the countless insects that crawl under the 
wet leaves and slick stones. 
The Wealdwoods are not only home to towering trees and the 
beasts that walk beneath them, numerous rivers, streams, and 
wetlands cut through much of these lands. Herds of baughur 
wallow through the shallows, covered in mud and chewing 
through root and vine, while the fast moving rapids are home to 
larkiera, their cartilaginous spines shearing through the water 
while their toothed maws snap up smaller fish. Much can be 
found by the waters edge here for a Traveler, and if fortunate, even 
a quite moment to put their fishing rod to use.

this fungus has a true symbiotic 
relationship with the beetle and is 
in bloom while the host still lives. 
A portion of its life cycle is spent 
protected on the beetle as the insect 
migrates to warmer locations.
